app.name: Pica
app.tagline: A thin Android voice client for Pipecat
app.packageIdNote: Historical; slated to be renamed as the app generalizes beyond the prototype.
app.thesis: The phone is just a great microphone and speaker with a nice UI. All intelligence — STT, LLM, TTS, turn-taking, barge-in — lives on a Pipecat server. Swapping the LLM or TTS voice is a server change the app never sees.
app.connectionModel: Direct peer-to-peer WebRTC using the official Pipecat Android SDK and the RTVI protocol. No JWT, no SFU, no rooms — signaling is 'POST an SDP offer to /api/offer'.
app.presentedAt: DroidKaigi 2026 (Tokyo), one of three sibling voice apps (Cliff = hand-wired cloud streaming; GVP = fully on-device; Pica = thin client over a Pipecat server).

designPrinciples.name: SDK isolation
designPrinciples.detail: The entire Pipecat SDK surface is quarantined in one file (net/PicaVoiceClient.kt) behind a transport-agnostic Listener interface. The major SDK jump (0.3.x -> 1.1.0, RTVI 1.0.0) touched exactly that one file — nothing else in the app moved.

designPrinciples.name: One backend live at a time
designPrinciples.detail: Switching agents tears the client fully down before bringing the next up. Two backend connections are never live at once.

designPrinciples.name: Server owns the pipeline
designPrinciples.detail: Everything except audio capture/playback lives on the server. The phone owns only the audio and the UI.

designPrinciples.name: Client-side latency truth
designPrinciples.detail: The headline latency number (silence -> first bot audio) is measured purely client-side, so it reflects what the user actually hears — not a server-reported metric.

layers.tech: libwebrtc capture/playback with AEC3; AudioManager routing
OkHttp 4 (URL parsing only); WebRTC owns the media path

modules.detail: Single-Activity root. Switches between three top-level states: live session, read-only history viewer, and idle setup screen (with the history drawer). Owns the app-root snackbar, mic/notification permission requests, keep-screen-on, and starts/stops the mic foreground service on sessionActive.

Owns the voice session across config changes. Implements PicaVoiceClient.Listener; maps RTVI events to AgentUiState, transcript persistence, orb amplitude, and the latency HUD. Manages the editable agent list, agent selection, speaker routing, and saved-conversation history.

Wraps PipecatClient + SmallWebRTCTransport. Translates PipecatEventCallbacks into the app's transport-agnostic Listener. connect() POSTs the SDP offer to the agent's URL verbatim; disconnect()/release() tear it down.

One selectable Pipecat backend: host, port, path (default /api/offer), scheme, label, accent, and visualizer (a VisualizerStyle key stored as a plain string so unknown/future keys degrade to the default instead of failing to deserialize). url and badge are derived. InitialAgents seeds the first three from BuildConfig; after seeding they are ordinary editable/deletable rows.

Enum of the session visualizers an agent can choose: SCOPE ('Oscilloscope', the default), BASES ('Running the Bases'), ORB ('Orange Orb'). Persisted on ServerEndpoint as its string key; fromKey() maps unknown keys to the default. Adding a style = one enum entry + one branch in VoiceAgentScreen; the editor's picker enumerates entries automatically.

Holds the FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MICROPHONE type so a live session survives the screen turning off or the app backgrounding. Does not capture audio itself — libwebrtc owns the mic; this just keeps the process promoted. START_STICKY.
Lazily builds the Room DB + ConversationRepository and the system AudioManager. No token client — Pica POSTs its SDP offer straight to the full offer URL.
Agent list + current selection + speaker preference, persisted as JSON in SharedPreferences.

ChatSession (with an agent snapshot: id/title/accent taken at creation) and MessageItem (keyed on transcript messageId). SessionDao + MessageDao. Only 'saved' sessions surface in the drawer; unsaved ones are purged at startup.
newSession (stamps agent snapshot), upsertMessage (incremental transcripts overwrite one row), savedSessions flow, save/rename/delete, and purgeUnsaved (startup crash-cleanup).

Agent list: select / add / edit / delete, and start session. The agent editor dialog includes a Visualizer radio list (enumerates VisualizerStyle.entries, so new styles appear without editor changes).

Transcript, speaker toggle, save FAB, latency HUD, visualizer toggle. Branches on the selected agent's VisualizerStyle to compose the scope, bases, or orb visualizer — the single switch point for styles.
Phosphor-scope trace — terminal green for the bot, cyan for the user — that pulses with live speech cadence.

Dodger-blue ballpark — outfield wall, foul lines, basepath, mound. A glowing runner sprints the bases while someone speaks, holds the nearest bag in silence, flashes bases on the way round, and scores runs on a scoreboard pill. Runner tint follows the speaker.

The Cliff app's additive amber/bronze particle-orb stack, ported to Pica's synthesized speech envelope; breathing, spread, spin rate and wobble track speech, with a warm/cool center bloom per speaker.
DisposableEffect: vm.connect() on enter, vm.disconnect() on dispose. Composed only while sessionActive is true.
Saved-conversation drawer (open / rename / delete) and a read-only transcript viewer with Android share-sheet export.

signalFlow.description: One P2P WebRTC/Opus connection carries audio both ways; RTVI events ride the same link as a side channel that drives the UI.

server.label: Pipecat server (the 'agent')
pipeline: the 'LLM' slot — Homer puts a whole OpenClaw agent here
server.note: The demo server (Homer) stack; the app never knows which components are used — any pipeline honoring the contract works. enable_metrics=True lets the server's latency breakdown line up with the client number.

sideChannel.label: RTVI events
drives: the agent's selected visualizer (scope / bases / orb)

visualizers.model: A per-agent choice, not a global setting: each ServerEndpoint persists a VisualizerStyle key, picked in the agent editor and switched on in VoiceAgentScreen when that agent's session runs.

styles.label: Oscilloscope
styles.note: The default; existing agents without a stored key resolve to it.

styles.label: Running the Bases
styles.note: Ballpark scene; runner sprints bases with speech, scores runs on a scoreboard.

styles.label: Orange Orb
styles.note: Additive amber/bronze orb ported from the Cliff sibling app.

visualizers.signal: All three are driven by the same synthesized speech envelope (level + speechPulse + activeSource) — the SmallWebRTC transport delivers no real audio levels, so amplitude is synthesized from RTVI speaking/transcript events.
visualizers.extension: Add a VisualizerStyle entry and one branch in VoiceAgentScreen; the editor's radio list and persistence need no changes. Unknown persisted keys degrade to the default.

sessionLifecycle.title: Start
sessionLifecycle.detail: SetupScreen -> startSession(). ViewModel creates a Room session row (with an agent snapshot), registers an AudioDeviceCallback for hot-plug routing, and flips sessionActive=true. MainActivity requests mic (+ notifications) permission, starts MicForegroundService, and keeps the screen on.

sessionLifecycle.title: Connect
sessionLifecycle.detail: PicaSessionHost is composed and calls vm.connect(). The ViewModel builds a fresh PicaVoiceClient bound to the selected agent's URL, then client.connect() POSTs the SDP offer to /api/offer; the server answers; ICE completes; media flows P2P.

sessionLifecycle.title: Bot speaks first
sessionLifecycle.detail: The server seeds a greeting on on_client_connected, so the user hears Pica before saying anything — confirming the loop is alive end to end.

sessionLifecycle.title: Converse
sessionLifecycle.detail: libwebrtc captures the mic (AEC3), encodes Opus, ships it to the server. RTVI events map to UI state: started/stopped speaking -> orb + scope tint + latency stopwatch; transcripts -> chat bubbles persisted to Room.

sessionLifecycle.title: Barge-in
sessionLifecycle.detail: Local TTS playback stops the instant the user speaks (onUserStartedSpeaking), before the server's VAD interrupt even round-trips. The server's interruption catches up.

sessionLifecycle.title: Stop
sessionLifecycle.detail: onDispose -> vm.disconnect() fully tears the client down (disconnect + release). stopSession() resets audio mode, unregisters the device callback, discards the session if unsaved, and stops the foreground service.

rtviEvents.usedFor: Session lifecycle. onDisconnected distinguishes an intentional stop from a mid-session drop (only the latter raises 'Connection lost').
Surfaces a snackbar 'Server error' while connected.
Sets activeSource=USER (tints the scope), and locally stops playback for barge-in.
Starts the silence->first-audio stopwatch (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime); sets isThinking=true.
Stops the stopwatch -> lastTurnMs (the latency HUD number); sets activeSource=BOT.
Clears activeSource; advances the bot transcript turn counter.
User chat bubbles — interim text replaces one row; final advances the id.
Assistant chat bubbles — sentence chunks accumulate within one turn. (Deprecated in 1.x in favor of onBotOutput; still fires.)
Wired to orb amplitude but NEVER fired by the SmallWebRTC 1.1.0 client — it emits no audio levels. Kept ready in case a future server sends them.

signaling.note: Produced/consumed by Pipecat's SmallWebRTCRequestHandler (server) and SmallWebRTCTransport (client) — don't hand-roll it. One offer per session.

audio.uplink: Mic -> server: Opus over WebRTC; server sees PCM after decode (STT 16 kHz).
audio.downlink: Server -> speaker: TTS PCM (24 kHz) encoded to Opus by the transport.
audio.aec: AEC3 is built into libwebrtc on BOTH ends — do not disable it, or the bot transcribes itself.

requiredServerBehaviors: Answer /api/offer and return the handler's answer verbatim.
Run an RTVIProcessor + RTVIObserver so the app gets speaking/transcript events.
Seed a greeting on on_client_connected (bot speaks first).
clientServerContract.notInV1: Voice selection. The app sends no voice ID; the server uses its configured CARTESIA_VOICE_ID. Runtime switching would need an RTVI custom message on both ends.

agentModel.definition: A Pipecat backend is just data: host + port + path (+ scheme), a label/accent, and a visualizer style. Every agent speaks the identical WebRTC+RTVI contract, so the ONLY thing that differs is the offer URL the transport POSTs to (plus cosmetics). Adding a backend is adding a row — no code.

seeds.title: OpenClaw
seeds.idea: The agentic backend — the conference demo (default)

agentModel.seedingNote: OPENCLAW_SERVER_URL is required by the build (build.gradle.kts fails fast if it's missing). After first launch the seed is an ordinary editable/deletable row — NOT recomputed from build config.

latencyHud.measurement: onUserStoppedSpeaking -> onBotStartedSpeaking, purely client-side, using SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() (monotonic, immune to wall-clock jumps).
latencyHud.purpose: The headline responsiveness number, per turn — what the user actually experiences, measured on the device.

behaviors: Transcripts are incremental: the same messageId grows from first word to full utterance; upsert overwrites one row.
Only explicitly saved sessions appear in the history drawer; auto-title from the first user turn.
purgeUnsaved() runs at startup so a crash/OS-kill can't leave junk sessions in the drawer.
The agent snapshot keeps saved history correctly labeled/colored even after the agent is renamed or deleted.

audioRouting.api31Plus: setCommunicationDevice over availableCommunicationDevices — speaker, or Bluetooth SCO / wired headset / earpiece by preference.
audioRouting.hotplug: AudioDeviceCallback re-applies routing when devices are added/removed mid-session.

knownQuirks: No client-side audio levels: the SmallWebRTC RTVI client never emits amplitude, so all three visualizers are event-driven — they animate on a synthesized envelope (speechPulse on transcript tokens + speaking start/stop) rather than true amplitude. The onUserAudioLevel/onRemoteAudioLevel hooks are wired but stay at 0.
Voice selection is server-side in v1 — the app sends no voice ID.
onBotTranscript is deprecated in the 1.x SDK (in favor of onBotOutput) but still fires; migrating is a follow-up, not part of the version bump.

referenceServer.name: Homer — the baseball voice agent
referenceServer.location: https://github.com/m15-ai/droidkaigi2026-homer-server — its own repo (part of the DroidKaigi 2026 demo hub).
referenceServer.stack: Deepgram Nova-3 STT -> an OpenClaw agent in the pipeline's LLM slot -> Cartesia Sonic-2 TTS, with VAD + interruptions. Answers MLB questions from live data (statsapi.mlb.com).
referenceServer.idea: The voice pipeline treats a whole agent as if it were just an LLM: the client, audio stack, and WebRTC contract never change — only the brain behind the LLM slot does.
referenceServer.note: Docs/ here holds only client-side docs (CLIENT_SERVER_CONTRACT.md is what any server must implement).
